survey: Image 4 shows a gold sheriff's star badge against a purple sunburst. Its parts: (1) a five-pointed star body with a raised outer rim, and each arm split into two bevelled facets along a centre ridge; (2) a gold ball on the tip of each of the five arms, each joined by a short neck; (3) a round gold bezel in the centre holding a domed red gem. The badge faces the camera almost head-on. It is turned a little within the picture and tipped very slightly, so the rim's thickness shows on the lower-right edges. The arms differ a little in length and spacing, but that is mild stylisation and fits the slight tip. The bezel and gem look close to circular, which matches a nearly face-on surface. The five balls are spheres of about the same size, shaded from the same light and seen from the same side. Each arm's centre ridge runs to its tip, and all facets agree on one view. There is no ground plane, so contact does not apply.
